title: Tallgrass AgriFlow onramp - field discovery & pilot notes
content:
Call capture: Tallgrass AgriFlow - discovery (02/19/2026)
Attendees: Riley (Redwood), Samir (Redwood SE), Laura (Tallgrass PM), Owen (Tallgrass Infra), Priya (Tallgrass Ops)

Topline: Tallgrass runs a distributed set of soil sensors + edge camera rigs across ~120 small-to-mid sized farms in the Midwest. They want a pilot that:
  - surfaces near-real-time crop health alerts (disease/stress) to field techs,
  - provides natural-lang explanations for anomalies ("why is this sensor spiking?"), and
  - optionally produces weekly summary reports for agronomists.

Constraints / must-haves noted by customer:
  - Data residency: some farms have EU-subsidiaries; any PII or personally identifiable farm contracts must be stored in-region (EU/US).
  - Intermittent connectivity: many sites have 10-60min sync windows per hour; edge-first strategy required.
  - Lightweight on-prem inference on small GPU/CPU edge boxes (NVIDIA T4/Jetson Xavier NX); fallback offline model for totally air-gapped sites.
  - Cost sensitivity: they estimate 3–5M events/month, want predictable unit economics for peak season.
  - Security: customers require KMS integration (Azure/AWS) and audit logs for all inference requests.

Technical requirements (first-pass):
  - Model surface: 1) Embeddings for time-series & camera metadata for reranking; 2) Small LLM (<= 7B quantized) for on-device reasoning/explanations; 3) Larger hosted variant (13B+) for aggregate weekly reports.
  - Storage: per-farm chunked vector store, sharded by region. Embedding dimensionality TBD (suggest 768/1024).
  - Sync semantics: edge boxes should queue events and perform local inference for alerting; periodic batch sync to private control plane to re-run heavy re-ranking/QA on hosted models.
  - Batching & latency: near-real-time alerts must be sub-800ms p95 on-device (inference only). Hosted async report generation can be >30s.
  - Caching: prefix/KV cache to avoid recomputing repeated queries (sensor drift use-cases).
  - Rollout: start with 10 farms, canary 2 farms, expand to 30, then 120. Need OTA model updates for edge.

Operational gotchas captured during call:
  - Edge hardware diversity: some farms use older Jetson deployments with intermittent reboots — need robust worker restart-state recovery and KV cache warmup strategies.
  - POS/ERP integration: Tallgrass wants to cross-reference sensor anomalies with harvest schedules (their ERP is a heavily customized 3rd-party). Integration will be messy; likely out-of-scope for MVP.
  - Data labeling: existing historical labels are noisy; suggested path: 1) small human-in-the-loop label set from agronomists, 2) active learning loop via Redwood Optimize telemetry.
  - Tokenization surprises: camera-captured OCR (equipment tags) produces mixed Unicode — need to normalize to NFC and strip non-printables prior to embedding.
  - Network policy: some farms block outbound traffic except via a proxy; private deployments must support proxy configuration and cert pinning.

Pilot success metrics (Tallgrass):
  - Precision of action-worthy alerts >= 80% (measured vs agronomist adjudication).
  - Time to alert: median <= 2 minutes from event at edge to field-tech notification (includes sensor processing + local inference + sync).
  - Monthly inference cost per farm under $X (they asked us to propose tiers).

Open questions (need answers before scope finalization):
  1) Exact edge hardware inventory and OS versions (Owen to share a CSV of boxes + network profile) — ACTION: Owen, due 2026-02-26.
  2) Data retention and GDPR specifics for EU farms (legal team to confirm whether pseudonymization is sufficient) — ACTION: Riley (R) to loop in security/compliance.
  3) Are there existing webhooks for their mobile app (field-tech) or do we need to propose push-notification infra? Laura to confirm mobile flow — ACTION: Laura, due 2026-02-27.
  4) Can Tallgrass accept a hybrid billing: reserved capacity for hosted weekly reports + usage for edge inferencing? Pricing team to draft options — ACTION: Finance contact (TBD).

Immediate internal TODOs (Redwood):
  - SE design spike: edge-first architecture diagram + failure modes (30% doc). Owner: Samir. Due: 2026-02-24.
  - Quantized model feasibility: run benchmark on Jetson Xavier NX for 7B fp16 vs int8 quantized. Owner: Owen (bench), Samir (interpret). Due: 2026-03-03.
  - Privacy mapping: draft short note on pseudonymization + region-based storage patterns. Owner: Riley + Security. Due: 2026-02-28.
  - Pricing ballpark for pilot (3 months, 10 farms): draft two options (hosted-heavy vs private-heavy). Owner: PMM. Due: 2026-03-01.

Integration notes / implementation ideas (brainstorm):
  - Local inference tiering: tiny on-device model for binary alerts (disease/no-disease), medium quantized model for short explanations, invoke hosted model for deep analysis. Automatic fallback chain when hosted unavailable.
  - Delta-sync strategy: only ship summaries + new embeddings during constrained windows; keep raw high-res imagery encrypted and uploaded during overnight windows.
  - Warm-start embeddings: prepopulate edge vector store with representative seasonal clusters so early queries are meaningful.
  - Canary update strategy: deploy model updates to a pool labelled "low-risk" (2 farms) with telemetry hooks to roll back within 1 hour if false-alerts spike > 10%.

Risk register (high-level):
  - False positives causing unnecessary field dispatches -> reputational risk. Mitigation: conservative thresholding + human-in-loop confirm for first 4 weeks.
  - Air-gapped sites missing critical updates -> ensure scheduled maintenance window + portable update USB fallback.
  - Unexpected load during harvest -> autoscaling for hosted re-ranking but need reserved capacity guarantees for peak.

Notes from Laura (customer) -- informal: "we want something pragmatic not research-y. If it prevents 1 wrong pesticide application a month per farm, we're already sold."

Proposed next steps (client-facing):
  1) Share SE spike doc + high-level architecture by 2026-02-24 (Samir).
  2) Quick feasibility bench results for 7B quant on Jetson by 2026-03-03 (Owen).
  3) Draft pilot SOW (3 months, 10 farms) with pricing options by 2026-03-05 (Riley + PMM).
  4) Schedule on-site/remote site audit window (1 day per region) — Laura to propose dates.

Back-of-envelope timeline (if pilot approved):
  - Week 0–2: infra + edge config, hardware validation
  - Week 3–6: model pruning/quant + embed tuning + local deploys
  - Week 7–10: canary + telemetry collection + threshold tuning
  - Week 11–12: expand to pilot cohort, handover docs

Quick links / references to include in SOW:
  - Redwood private deployment options (VPC + on-prem)
  - OTA rollout + rollback examples (canary strategy)
  - Redwood Optimize: active learning loop suggestion

Internal thoughts / scribbles:
  - Consider offering a small "edge appliance" SKU for Tallgrass (tied to reserved commitment). Might simplify support.
  - Explore partnership with regional MSP for on-site maintenance during harvest.

End of notes.

-- Riley (R)
  raw capture for internal SE follow-up.
